footer.tagline: A physical status light for your coding agent.

home.title: Know your agent's state without staring at a terminal.
home.subtitle: A physical desktop status light for Claude Code and CLI coding agents — green, yellow, red, at a glance.
home.stripAriaLabel: Simulated status light cycling through idle, working, waiting, and compacting states

whatItIs.heading: A status light you don't have to look for.
whatItIs.body: Ten addressable LEDs behind a diffuser, wired to a USB-C dev board, driven by a small Python CLI. Claude Code hooks flip its color automatically — green while the agent's working, yellow when it's waiting on you, red when it's idle. No dashboard, no extra window.

whyItExists.heading: Built for the tab you keep checking.
whyItExists.body: Coding agents run in the background, but "in the background" still means glancing at a terminal window every few minutes to check if it's stuck waiting on you. This moves that one bit of information off the screen entirely — walk away, glance at the light, know exactly where things stand.

waiting.label: Waiting
waiting.description: It needs you — a permission or an answer.

openHardware.heading: Open hardware, honestly a hobby project.
openHardware.body: MIT-licensed — schematics, firmware, and CLI all included. Five units built and tested, Linux and Windows supported today. Not a commercial product, not for sale. Built because a physical light is more fun to build, and more useful to have, than another terminal tab.

overview.heading: What's actually on the desk
overview.body: A Waveshare RP2040-Zero, hand-soldered onto a custom PCB, driving 10 addressable WS2812B LEDs behind a 3D-printed diffuser. One USB-C cable carries both power and the serial connection back to your machine — no separate power supply, no wireless pairing, nothing to configure beyond installing the CLI.
overview.diagramAriaLabel: Diagram of the board: an RP2040-Zero, a USB-C connector, and a row of 10 addressable LEDs split into a status pixel plus green, yellow, and red sections

howItWorks.heading: One character, one color
howItWorks.body: The host CLI talks to the firmware over USB serial with about the simplest protocol that could work: a single ASCII character plus a newline. No JSON, no handshake.

reliability.heading: Built to be trusted while you're not looking
reliability.body: A 30-minute watchdog runs on the firmware itself — if it stops hearing from the host, the red section switches from solid to a slow breathing pulse instead of freezing on a stale color. A status light you walk away from has to fail visibly, not silently.

hooks.heading: Wired straight into Claude Code
hooks.body: Claude Code hooks call the CLI directly and synchronously — not async — so the light always reflects the true order of events, even through a tool-call-heavy turn.

openSource.heading: Nothing hidden
openSource.body: MIT-licensed, start to finish — schematics, firmware, host CLI, and the hook config it installs. The full bill of materials and build guide are in the docs if you want to build your own.

fieldNotes.heading: Where it stands
fieldNotes.body: Five units built and tested. Linux is a one-line pipx install; Windows has a one-click (unsigned) installer. macOS isn't supported yet. This is a hobby project, not a commercial product — no roadmap promises, just what's actually working today.
